entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0333: Resource budgets not enforced on the typed deserialization path
entry.content:
Resource budgets not enforced on the typed deserialization path

Aliases: GHSA-4xcc-23fx-w2wj

Affected:

  • noyalib — fixed in 0.0.53

`ParserConfig::max_events`, `max_nodes`, `max_total_scalar_bytes`, `max_merge_keys`, `alias_anchor_ratio` and the alias jump factor were enforced only by the two `Value` loaders. A typed target with a default-shaped configuration is served by the streaming deserializer, which never read those fields, so tightening any of them had no effect on `from_str::<T>` for a struct target. The default document-length, depth and alias-count caps were enforced on every path, so no input was unbounded; the gap affects callers who tightened the other budgets for hostile input. Version 0.0.53 charges every budget on the streaming path as well and adds cross-path parity tests. Users who cannot upgrade can deserialize into `noyalib::Value` first and convert with `from_value`, or rely on `max_document_leng…

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/noyalib
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0333.html
  • https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/noyalib/pull/470

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0332: `WaveFormat::parse` reads past the end of a `&WAVEFORMATEX`
entry.content:
`WaveFormat::parse` reads past the end of a `&WAVEFORMATEX`

Affected:

  • wasapi — fixed in 0.25.0

`WaveFormat::parse` is a safe function that takes a `&WAVEFORMATEX`, which is only valid for reads of `size_of::<WAVEFORMATEX>()` (18) bytes. When the header has `wFormatTag == WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE` and `cbSize >= 22`, the function reinterprets the reference as a `WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE` and reads 40 bytes. Nothing in the signature guarantees that the header sits at the start of a larger buffer, so safe code can trigger an out-of-bounds read: ```rust use wasapi::WaveFormat; use windows::Win32::Media::Audio::WAVEFORMATEX; use windows::Win32::Media::KernelStreaming::WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE; let header = WAVEFORMATEX { wFormatTag: WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE as u16, nChannels: 2, nSamplesPerSec: 48000, nAvgBytesPerSec: 384000, nBlockAlign: 8, wBitsPerSample: 32, cbSize…

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/wasapi
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0332.html
  • https://github.com/HEnquist/wasapi-rs/issues/65
  • https://github.com/HEnquist/wasapi-rs/pull/64

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0331: Panic on Decoding Short Hybrid Keys

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0329: Auto-Reseeding HMAC-DRBG could panic for some output lengths
entry.content:
Auto-Reseeding HMAC-DRBG could panic for some output lengths

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • libcrux-hmac-drbg — fixed in 0.0.2

The automatically reseeding implementations of HMAC-DRBG would panic if called with a desired non-zero output length cleanly divisible by `65_536`, the maximum number of output bytes that can be generated before reseeding has to happen. # Impact An application relying on `libcrux-hmac-drgb` to provide randomness of byte length a non-zero integer multiple of `65_536` in a single call to `fill_bytes` would panic. Any calls with output buffer lengths not cleanly divisible by `65_536` are not affected. # Mitigation With release the release of version `0.0.2` of `libcrux-hmac-drbg` this bug has been fixed and reseeding DRBG implementations can be used with arbitrary output lengths. We recommend users upgrade to `libcrux-hmac-drbg` version `0.0.2`.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/libcrux-hmac-drbg
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0329.html

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-pmfc-4wjj-gmhx: cut: -s ignored in -z -d '' newline-delimiter mode
entry.content:
cut: -s ignored in -z -d '' newline-delimiter mode

Aliases: CVE-2026-35381

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • uu_cut — fixed in 0.8.0

`cut` routes `-z -d ''` through a special newline-delimiter path that ignores the `-s` only-delimited flag, emitting whole undelimited records (plus NUL) that should be suppressed. Pipelines relying on `cut -s` to drop undelimited records process data that should be filtered. ``` printf 'abc' | cut -z -d '' -s -f 1 | od -An -tx1 # GNU: no output ; uutils: 61 62 63 00 ``` --- _Zellic private finding (zellic-ext/coreutils-private PR #102). Reported in the Zellic *uutils coreutils Program Security Assessment* (for Canonical, Jan 2026), audited commit `3a07ffc5a9bd4c283e75afa548ba1f1957bad242`._

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2cv4-cqwr-gwf7: uv: Path traversal on Windows through wheel extraction
entry.content:
uv: Path traversal on Windows through wheel extraction

Aliases: CVE-2026-104843

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • uv — fixed in 0.12.18
  • uv — fixed in 0.12.18

### Impact In versions of uv from 0.12.7 to 0.12.18 on Windows, uv could be induced into writing a file outside of the installation prefix during wheel installation. A malicious wheel could use this to place an executable outside of the intended environment, including in a directory already present on the user's PATH. This vulnerability only affects Windows hosts; no other platforms are affected. ### Patches uv 0.12.18 and newer address this vulnerability. Users are encouraged to upgrade to 0.12.18. ### Workarounds There is no workaround other than upgrading to uv 0.12.18.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc: Rustls: TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across encryption level boundaries
entry.content:
Rustls: TLS 1.3 handshake messages incorrectly accepted across encryption level boundaries

Aliases: RUSTSEC-2026-0285

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.45

Rustls accepted TLS 1.3 handshake messages sent at the wrong encryption level when they followed a key-changing message in the same record. The handshake transcript is still authenticated, so a network-position attacker cannot use this to alter or complete a handshake; the practical effect is that a peer could send handshake messages that should be encrypted in plaintext without rustls rejecting the connection. This issue affects rustls versions 0.23.13 through 0.23.44 inclusive. # Original report ### Summary Rustls (tested version 0.23.44, and it appears still an issue on latest master though I have not tested this) accepts a TLS 1.3 server flight where a plaintext EncryptedExtensions is packed into the same record as the ServerHello. This is very similar to Go's CVE-2025-61730 fixed i…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-6w6g-hm98-mhgm: hickory-resolver: Unbounded TC-retry loop in `NameServerPool::try_send` (resource-exhaustion DoS)
entry.content:
hickory-resolver: Unbounded TC-retry loop in `NameServerPool::try_send` (resource-exhaustion DoS)

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • hickory-resolver — fixed in 0.26.2

When the `hickory-resolver` name server pool implementation receives an upstream response with the TC (truncated) header bit set, it re-queues the request to the same nameserver to retry with UDP transport disabled. However, the retry arm never inspects the transport that just answered and carries no iteration counter. An authoritative server that sets `TC=1` on **every** available transport keeps the resolver spinning on one persistent TCP connection until the 5s per-request wall-clock deadline expires. ### Reporter Qifan Zhang, Palo Alto Networks

References:

  • https://github.com/hickory-dns/hickory-dns/security/advisories/GHSA-6w6g-hm98-mhgm

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-6f2x-v7q7-m7m5: hickory-resolver follows irrelevant CNAME records
entry.content:
hickory-resolver follows irrelevant CNAME records

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • hickory-resolver — fixed in 0.26.2

When the Hickory DNS resolver follows CNAME records, it sends queries that are not necessary to answer the original recursive query. If there are any CNAME records in the authority section or additional section of the response, queries will be sent for those names. If there are any CNAME records that are not part of a CNAME chain starting from the original recursive query name, queries will be sent for those names. This increases query amplification beyond what is necessary to answer the recursive query.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-5j98-2g5x-46v6: hickory-resolver: Resolver::lookup() and Resolver::lookup_ip() APIs obscure DNSSEC validation failures
entry.content:
hickory-resolver: Resolver::lookup() and Resolver::lookup_ip() APIs obscure DNSSEC validation failures

Aliases: CVE-2026-93657

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • hickory-resolver — fixed in 0.26.2

When calling `Resolver::lookup()` or `Resolver::lookup_ip()` on a resolver with DNSSEC validation enabled, both methods return `Ok(...)` if DNSSEC validation fails. It is possible but very inconvenient to check the validation status of individual records. These methods should instead return an error when DNSSEC validation determines a response is bogus.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2024-0448: `parse_arguments` reads a caller-supplied pointer as a slice
entry.content:
`parse_arguments` reads a caller-supplied pointer as a slice

Affected:

  • rutie — fixed in 0.10.3, 0.11.3, 0.12.1, 0.13.1, 0.14.1

`parse_arguments` is safe. It takes `arguments: *const AnyObject` and `argc`, and calls `slice::from_raw_parts(arguments, argc as usize)`. It does not check that `arguments` is non-null and aligned, or that `argc` elements are initialized. Safe Rust can pass a null pointer or a length past the allocation. The maintainer confirmed this on 2026-10-03, including a debug abort on Rust 1.78+ when Ruby calls an arity -1 method (`to_s` via `format`, `puts`, or `Array#join`) with a NULL `argv` and `argc` of 0.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/rutie
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0448.html
  • https://github.com/danielpclark/rutie/issues/190

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0328: `decompress`: tar-family extractors write archive entries without a path-traversal check (tar-slip)
entry.content:
`decompress`: tar-family extractors write archive entries without a path-traversal check (tar-slip)

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • decompress

The tar-family extractors in `decompress` (`.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.xz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.zst`) build each output path from the **raw archive entry path** and write to it with no traversal check, so a malicious archive can write files **outside** the destination directory, a "tar-slip" / zip-slip path traversal (CWE-22 / CWE-23). In `src/decompressors/tar_common.rs` (`tar_extract`): ```rust let filepath = entry.path()?; // raw entry path let filepath = filepath.components().skip(opts.strip).collect::<PathBuf>(); // strips leading components only — keeps `..` let outpath = to.join(filepath); // ... let mut outfile = fs::File::create(&outpath)?; // writes anywhere ``` `.components().skip(opts.strip)…

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/decompress
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0328.html
  • https://github.com/rusty-ferris-club/decompress/issues/21

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-pvmv-cwg8-v6c8: Zebra v4.4.0 still accepts V5 SIGHASH_SINGLE without a corresponding output
entry.content:
Zebra v4.4.0 still accepts V5 SIGHASH_SINGLE without a corresponding output

Aliases: CVE-2026-104435

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:H/SA:H

Affected:

  • zebrad — fixed in 4.4.1
  • zebra-script — fixed in 6.0.1

# Consensus Divergence in V5 Transparent SIGHASH_SINGLE With No Corresponding Output ## Summary Zebra failed to enforce a ZIP-244 consensus rule for V5 transparent transactions: when an input is signed with `SIGHASH_SINGLE` and there is no transparent output at the same index as that input, validation must fail. Zebra instead asked the underlying sighash library to compute a digest, and that library produced a digest over an empty output set rather than failing. An attacker could craft a V5 transaction with more transparent inputs than outputs that Zebra accepts but `zcashd` rejects, creating a consensus split between Zebra and `zcashd` nodes. A previous fix ([`GHSA-cwfq-rfcr-8hmp`](https://github.com/ZcashFoundation/zebra/security/advisories/GHSA-cwfq-rfcr-8hmp)) addressed a closely re…
